what.text: Melatonin is a hormone the body makes, mainly at night, that helps run the sleep-wake cycle. Most melatonin products are made synthetically.

src.label: Melatonin: what you need to know, NIH NCCIH

what.text: Taken by mouth, melatonin is used for sleep. In the US it is sold as a dietary supplement. In the EU, prolonged-release melatonin tablets are prescription medicines: Circadin for short-term insomnia in people 55 and over, and Slenyto for insomnia in children and teens with autism, certain genetic conditions or ADHD.

what.text: Using melatonin on the scalp for hair loss is off-label. Melatonin by mouth for sleep is sold as a supplement in the US and is an approved prescription medicine only in some countries.

research.text: For hair loss, one small randomized trial and a set of open, uncontrolled studies have tested melatonin solution on the scalp. For sleep, melatonin by mouth has been tested in many placebo-controlled trials; meta-analyses find small effects on how fast people fall asleep and on sleep quality.

research.title: Melatonin 0.1% scalp solution in women

facts.v: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot
40 women with pattern hair loss or diffuse hair loss
6 months
Share of growing (anagen) and resting (telogen) hairs on trichograms; blood melatonin

research.found: Melatonin raised the share of growing hairs at the back of the scalp in women with pattern hair loss (12 women) and at the front in women with diffuse hair loss (28 women). Other sites rose but not significantly. Blood melatonin rose but stayed below the normal night peak.

src.label: Fischer et al., Br J Dermatol, 2004

research.title: A cosmetic melatonin solution in men and women

facts.v: One drug-level study and four before-and-after studies, without placebo groups
Groups of 30, 35 and 60 people, and over 1,800 volunteers at 200 centers
Up to 6 months
Questionnaires, hair density by imaging, hair counts and hair-pull tests

research.found: The authors reported improvement in each study and good tolerance. Without placebo groups, these studies cannot show whether melatonin caused the changes.

src.label: Fischer et al., Int J Trichology, 2012

research.title: Melatonin for primary sleep disorders, 2013

facts.v: meta-analysis of randomized, placebo-controlled trials
19 trials, 1,683 adults and children with primary sleep disorders
varied
time to fall asleep, total sleep time, sleep quality

research.found: Melatonin cut time to fall asleep by about 7 minutes and added about 8 minutes of sleep vs. placebo, and sleep quality improved. The authors called the effects modest; they did not fade with continued use. Effects were larger in longer trials and at higher doses.

src.label: Ferracioli-Oda et al., PLoS One, 2013 (meta-analysis)

research.title: Melatonin and ramelteon for insomnia disorder, 2023

facts.v: systematic review and meta-analysis vs. placebo
22 studies, 4,875 participants (925 on melatonin, mostly prolonged-release)
short- and long-term
self-rated and lab-measured time to fall asleep, total sleep time, sleep efficiency

research.found: Prolonged-release melatonin cut time to fall asleep by about 5 to 6 minutes and raised sleep efficiency by about 2 percentage points, small to medium effects. Effects on sleep efficiency were larger when patients’ mean age was 55 or more.

src.label: Maruani et al., J Sleep Res, 2023 (meta-analysis)

research.title: Prolonged-release melatonin (Circadin) in people aged 55 to 80

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, after a 2-week placebo run-in; primary care in the West of Scotland
354 men and women aged 55 to 80 with primary insomnia
3 weeks
responders with better sleep quality and morning alertness (Leeds questionnaire); sleep index; time to fall asleep; quality of life

research.found: 26% on melatonin vs. 15% on placebo were responders. Time to fall asleep fell by 24 minutes vs. 13 minutes.

src.label: Wade et al., Curr Med Res Opin, 2007

research.title: Prolonged-release melatonin in insomnia patients 55 and over

facts.v: multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled
170 outpatients aged 55 and over with primary insomnia
3 weeks, then a check for rebound and withdrawal
sleep quality and morning alertness questionnaires

research.found: Sleep quality and morning alertness improved more than with placebo. No rebound insomnia or withdrawal effects were seen after stopping. Side effects were few and mostly minor.

src.label: Lemoine et al., J Sleep Res, 2007

research.title: Slenyto in children with autism or Smith-Magenis syndrome

facts.v: main placebo-controlled study behind Slenyto’s EU approval
125 children aged 2 to 17 (121 with autism, 4 with Smith-Magenis syndrome) who had tried sleep routines
13 weeks
total sleep time and time to fall asleep

research.found: Children on Slenyto slept 51 more minutes per night vs. 19 more on placebo, and fell asleep about 38 minutes earlier vs. 13 minutes on placebo.

us.text: In the US, melatonin is sold as a dietary supplement. No melatonin product is FDA approved, for sleep or for hair loss. As of November 1, 2026.
Compounded drugs are not FDA approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

side.text: No label covers melatonin on the scalp. The side effects below are for melatonin taken by mouth, from NIH, EMA and the sleep trials.

items.text: Short-term studies in adults reported mild effects: headache, dizziness, nausea and sleepiness. Long-term effects are unclear.

unconfirmed: We could not open Health Canada’s natural health product records for melatonin; only the prescription drug Slenyto was confirmed.
We did not confirm whether low-dose melatonin food supplements are allowed in individual EU countries.
We could not reach Australia’s TGA (ARTG search failed), so Australia is pending.
Health Canada’s approved indication for Slenyto was not opened; only its marketed status and prescription schedule were confirmed.
The funding of the 2007 Circadin trials (Wade, Lemoine) is not stated in the abstracts and the full papers were not opened.
Circadin’s status in the UK (MHRA) was not confirmed from an MHRA product record.
surprises: Melatonin is sold freely as a supplement in the US, but the UK’s MHRA treats it as a prescription-only medicine and has pulled a supplement found to contain it.
Most of the hair research on topical melatonin is open studies of a cosmetic solution without placebo groups; only one small placebo-controlled trial (40 women, 2004) was found.

Melatonin is an approved prescription sleep medicine in the EU (Circadin since 2007, Slenyto since 2018) and in Canada (Slenyto, marketed since July 2026), but in the US it has no FDA approval and is sold only as a supplement.
